$comment: Benevolence (decisions D-benevolence-1 to D-benevolence-4): who asked the church for help, who worked each request, and what the church gave. Each request is saved the way Rock's Benevolence Request Detail block saves it: the requester's name, email, phones, home address, connection status, and campus copied onto the request, a case worker from RSR - Benevolence, a status, and results with amounts. Requesters are people already in the data. No government ID is ever recorded, and gifts are results on the request, not gifts from a fund.

types.$comment: Rock's default type. It keeps its name and description and takes no new requests.

types.name: Rent and Utilities
types.description: Help with rent, a utility bill, or a deposit, paid straight to the landlord or the utility company.

types.name: Food and Essentials
types.description: Grocery and essentials gift cards, and the food pantry for help that lasts past one week.

types.name: Car and Medical
types.description: A car repair that keeps someone working, or a prescription or medical bill, paid straight to the shop or the provider.

$securityComment: Rock locks its benevolence pages to RSR - Benevolence and RSR - Rock Administration. Each type is locked to the same two roles, so a request shows only to them on every screen that checks the request, such as a person's Benevolence tab (decision D-benevolence-2).
$accessComment: The security walkthrough's benevolence questions, which verify asks Rock's own security check: Rock's Benevolence page under Finance, and each type a request inherits its security from.

caseWorker.name: Dee Navarro
caseWorker.$comment: The Care Director works every request. She is in RSR - Benevolence, the role Rock's case worker list reads.

generated.$comment: About 2 requests a year for every 1,000 active adults in the generated households, over the history window (decision D-benevolence-3). Requesters lean toward people the church knows but who are not yet deeply involved, one request per family. Requests from the last two weeks wait as Pending. Older ones are mostly Approved, some Denied.

$resultsComment: What the team gives for each type when it approves a request: Rock's result type, its weight, and the amount's range in dollars, or no amount for a referral.

The past-due utility bill, paid to the utility company.

text.$comment: Short pools for generated requests: what the person asked for by type, and what the team wrote when it decided.

rent-utilities: Rent is due on the first and I am short after a slow month at work.
Our electric bill went up with the heat and we got a shutoff notice.
I was out sick for two weeks without pay and fell behind on rent.
The water bill is past due after I missed shifts with a sick kid.
We moved for a new job and need help with the deposit.
My hours were cut and the gas bill is two months behind.
food-essentials: Money is tight until my next paycheck and we are low on groceries.
I lost my job last week and need help with food for my kids.
We need diapers and formula to get through the month.
My hours were cut and I could use help with groceries this month.
We just took in my sister's kids and the grocery bill doubled.
car-medical: My car needs a new alternator and I need it to get to work.
I need help with a prescription my insurance does not fully cover.
The car failed inspection and I drive forty minutes each way to work.
We have a clinic bill we cannot pay all at once.
My brakes are going and I drive my kids to school every day.

nextSteps: Shared the dates of the Money Matters budgeting class.
Invited them to meet with a volunteer budget coach.
Shared the job board and résumé help night.
Connected them with a small group near their home.
Prayed with them and will check in next month.
denied: We were not able to help with this request. Shared a list of community agencies.
The team helped this family earlier this year, so we referred them to a county assistance program.
We could not reach them to finish the request after several calls.
The request was larger than the fund allows. Shared other local resources.

agreement.$comment: The assistance agreement each approved rent, utility, car, or medical request has as a document: a one-page PDF the requester signs with the case worker.
agreement.title: Benevolence Assistance Agreement
paragraphs: {church} is glad to help with the need described below. The help is a gift, not a loan, and there is nothing to repay.
The church pays the landlord, company, or provider directly. No cash is given to the requester.
The requester agrees to meet with the case worker once more within 30 days to talk about next steps, such as a budgeting class or other help in the community.
The church keeps this request private. Only the benevolence team and the church's administrators can see it.
